transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I’m not sure it’s a big thing, and I don’t want to sound... unreasonable. It’s just that for about the past year I’ve been noticing things with my wife’s work—late meetings, little changes in her messages—and she says it’s all normal office stuff. Maybe it is.

But the timing of it all has felt a little too exact, like the things line up in a way that doesn’t seem accidental. Almost like there’s some private signal in it, something she’s trying to tell me without saying it directly. I know that probably sounds strange. I just thought maybe talking to someone would be the right thing to do.
Do you think it’s possible you might be mistaken about your wife sending you hidden signals?

I mean... yes, I suppose it’s possible. I don’t want to be closed-minded about it, and I know she says the late meetings and the changes in her work messages are just normal office things.

It’s just that over the past year, they’ve lined up so precisely sometimes that it’s hard for me to believe it’s accidental. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without actually saying it. I know that may not be the right way to look at it, but that’s how it’s felt to me.
Do you believe for certain that your wife is sending you hidden messages?

Certain is maybe a strong word... I don’t want to insist on something if that sounds unreasonable.

But honestly, yes, a lot of the time it feels that way to me. I know my wife says the late meetings and little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, but for the past year they’ve lined up too precisely to feel accidental. It’s like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly. Does that make sense?
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, not voices like someone talking when no one’s there. I haven’t noticed anything like that, at least. If I’m understanding what you mean correctly.
Have you felt that your thoughts were being put into your mind or taken out of it by someone or something?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve worried about things, obviously, but I haven’t felt like someone was literally putting thoughts in my head or taking them out. That doesn’t sound like what I’ve experienced, if I’m answering that the right way.
Before this past year, have you generally tended to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t think so, not generally. I mean, I’ve always tried to be careful about people’s intentions, like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say I went around assuming the worst of everyone.

At least, I hope I didn’t come across that way. Before this, I think I was pretty reasonable with people.
Have you ever felt that something outside you was controlling your actions or movements?

No, I don’t believe so. I’ve felt stressed or like things were out of my hands at times, but not like something outside of me was actually controlling my body or making me move. That’s not something I’ve noticed.
Have you had any neurological illness or brain injury?
Not that I’m aware of, no. I haven’t had anything like a brain injury or a neurological illness diagnosed. I mean, as far as I know, anyway.
Aside from your wife, do you believe anyone else is trying to send you hidden messages or communicate with you indirectly?

No… not anyone else, really. I don’t think strangers or other people are trying to reach me that way.

It’s mostly with my wife. I know she says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and maybe that sounds more reasonable, but over the past year they’ve lined up so precisely that it’s hard for me to see it as accidental. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly. Does that make sense?
Did this belief about your wife start suddenly?

Not suddenly, no… I mean, not like one day everything changed. It’s been more gradual, I think. About a year or so, since my wife started working outside the home again. At first I probably didn’t make much of it, but over time I started noticing it more.
Have your emotions been changing very quickly from one moment to the next during this period?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’ve been worried at times, but not like my emotions are flipping suddenly from one thing to another. At least I haven’t noticed that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Over this past year, have you found yourself becoming less able to manage your work or daily responsibilities than before?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m still getting to my teaching sections, keeping up with the data analysis, riding my bike, seeing friends for chess… so I wouldn’t say I’ve fallen apart or anything.

The main trouble is more at home, honestly. My wife and I can get stuck arguing about what her work schedule really means. But day to day, I think I’m managing pretty well. That sounds fair, right?
Do you believe your wife is deliberately using those work messages and schedule changes to send you coded messages meant specifically for you?

I wouldn’t put it as… deliberately, exactly. I know she says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and maybe that’s how it looks from the outside.

But over the past year, some of it has lined up too precisely to feel accidental to me. It’s like there’s a private signal in the timing or the wording, meant for me, to tell me something she isn’t saying directly. I know that probably sounds strange… I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is. But that is how it feels.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?

No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been seeing things that other people couldn’t see, at least not that I’m aware of. My eyes are fine, and I’m not… you know, seeing people or shapes or anything like that. Is that what you mean?
Over the past year, have you found yourself losing interest or motivation in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, maybe I get distracted sometimes, but I still enjoy the same things when I make time for them. Chess is still fun, biking helps clear my head, and my work is still interesting enough.

So… I wouldn’t say I’ve lost motivation in any major way. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have other people told you that your speech or your thinking has seemed confused or hard to follow?

No, not really. I mean, nobody’s told me that I’m hard to follow or that I sound confused. Sometimes my wife says I’m “reading too much into things,” but that’s not the same as my speech being jumbled or anything.

I try to be clear when I explain myself. If I’m not making sense here, you’d tell me, right?
Do you believe your wife is being unfaithful to you?

I… I don’t want to make her sound bad. She says the late meetings and the small changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and maybe that’s how it looks to other people.

But over the past year, it’s felt like they line up too precisely to be accidental. Like there’s some private signal in them, something she’s trying to tell me without saying it directly. I know that may sound… suspicious, and I’m not trying to accuse her unfairly. But yes, part of me does believe there’s something going on.
Do you ever feel that television, radio, or things you read are sending special messages meant specifically for you?

Not television or radio, no… I don’t think anything like that.

It’s more with my wife’s work messages, if I’m being honest. She says the late meetings and little changes in how she writes things are just normal office stuff, and I’m sure that’s what it looks like from the outside. But over the past year, sometimes they’ve lined up so precisely that it doesn’t feel accidental. It feels like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

I know that may sound like I’m overinterpreting it. I’m not trying to be difficult. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you become noticeably less emotionally expressive than you used to be?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I’m probably a little more serious lately, but I still laugh with people, I still show when I’m happy or upset.

My wife might say I’ve been preoccupied sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve become flat or anything like that. Does that answer what you mean?
If your wife showed you clear proof that these patterns were just ordinary work matters, would you be able to accept that you were mistaken?

I’d like to think I could, yes. I don’t want to be the kind of person who ignores clear proof.

But… I suppose it would depend on what it was. Because she does say the late meetings and the small changes in her work messages are just ordinary office things, and I understand that’s possible. It’s just that for the past year they’ve lined up so precisely sometimes that it’s hard for me to feel like it’s all accidental. It feels like there’s some private signal in there, like something she’s trying to tell me without saying it directly.

I know that probably sounds like I’m being stubborn. I’m not trying to be. I’d want to accept proof if it was clear enough.
